html:
The Sana were a small Indigenous people of central Texas, recorded in the 1600s and 1700s in the country between the Guadalupe and Brazos rivers. Their language is known only from a short list of words and is thought to be related to Tonkawa, though some scholars count them among the Coahuiltecan peoples.

In the 1700s many Sana entered the Spanish missions at San Antonio, above all Mission San Antonio de Valero, later famous as the Alamo. There they lived and married alongside many other groups, and by about 1800 they no longer appear in the records as a separate people.
